subject: Electrical Engineering
title: BIBO Stability: Bounded Input, Bounded Output
description: A short lesson to help you apply BIBO Stability: Bounded Input, Bounded Output.

hook.text: A stable system produces a bounded output for every bounded input. Unstable systems blow up.

buildup.text: Push a spring and it returns to rest — stable. Push a ball off a hilltop and it rolls away — unstable.

discovery.text: For linear systems, stability depends on pole locations. Left-half-plane poles mean stability.

twist.text: A pole exactly on the imaginary axis means marginal stability — the output oscillates forever without growing.

climax.text: Aircraft, power grids, and nuclear reactors are designed with large stability margins — no risks allowed.

punchline.text: Bounded in, bounded out — stability is the non-negotiable minimum.

quiz.question: Where must the poles of a stable linear system be located?
options: On the imaginary axis of the s-plane
In the left-half of the s-plane (negative real parts)
In the right-half of the s-plane (positive real parts)
